title: Destinies - App-based Adventure Time!
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YA_LFvsyLoU

Daniel (@dungeondive) skipped Destinies on Kickstarter — competitive story-driven campaign games had worn thin — and then bought it anyway after a month of Dungeon Dive Facebook group enthusiasm. Solo, it did nothing for him. With his regular Mansions of Madness group, four players sharing three characters, it was a fantastic night.

The app carries the game: read aloud, scan QR codes, build the village tile by tile. Each of the witch, huntsman and noble has two destinies, and the clue on the back of your character card is the only genuinely hidden information — everything else is public performance. Skill checks roll 2d6 against a track of tokens you slide downward with experience, with rechargeable fate dice hoarded for the big rolls. What Daniel singles out is the item scanning: he used a sword and an herb in ways he assumed the game would refuse, and it accommodated both. Most adventure games demand the exact right object; this one rewards lateral thinking.

His complaint is the plastic. The miniatures are so small and numerous the group repeatedly moved the wrong one, they add no tactical dimension, and the expansion ships in a base-game-sized box less than a quarter full because of one figure. He recommends the game, and asks Lucky Duck to have faith in it without the trinkets.

----

Have you ever loved a game enough to keep it despite the components — or has box bloat ever talked you out of a purchase you otherwise wanted?
